title: Lesson 33 - Virtualized data fundamentals: External Objects, Salesforce Connect, Data Connect
description: Given a customer scenario, decide when to use virtualized data and describe virtualized data options, including External Objects, Salesforce Connect adapters (OData, cross-org, etc.), and Data Connect for data sharing without copying.

questions.question: A company must show real-time inventory from a remote OData service in Salesforce without storing it, and the data changes constantly. Which approach fits?
options: Copy the data nightly into a custom object
Virtualize it as an External Object via Salesforce Connect (OData adapter)
Move Salesforce to a Big Object
Store inventory in a Big Object and query it
questions.explanation: Virtualization avoids staleness and copies for volatile remote data; nightly copy (A) is stale, and Big Objects (C, D) do not virtualize external sources.

questions.question: Which TWO are constraints of External Objects?
options: They require an External ID as the external key
They cannot be the child in a master-detail with standard objects
They are always faster than native objects
questions.explanation: External Objects need an External ID (A) and cannot be the child of a master-detail with standard objects (C); they do not support roll-ups (B) and are not inherently faster (D).

questions.question: When does copying beat virtualization in an LDV scenario?
options: When the data must remain only in the source for residency
When the platform needs native speed, validation, automation, and reporting on stable data
When the external source is slow and volatile
When the data changes every second
questions.explanation: Copy stable data when the platform must own it for speed/validation/reporting; residency (A) and volatile/slow-source cases (C, D) favor virtualization.
